# shopify_metaobject (Data Source)

Reads one metaobject entry by type and handle, for example to reference its `id` from a metafield value or a collection condition. Works for entries of Shopify-owned types (`shopify--…`) and merchant-owned types. Fails if no such entry exists. Entries are content that merchants edit in the admin; the data source reads the current state on every plan.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An entry of a Shopify standard type, read by type and handle.
data "shopify_metaobject" "material" {
  type   = "shopify--material"
  handle = "baumwolle"
}

output "material_id" {
  value = data.shopify_metaobject.material.id
}

output "material_label" {
  value = data.shopify_metaobject.material.fields["label"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `handle` (String) Entry handle, unique within the type.
- `type` (String) Definition type, e.g. `shopify--material`, exactly as the API returns it. A type of the provider's own app can also be given as `$app:<name>`.

### Read-Only

- `display_name` (String) The entry's label: the value of the display-name field, or Shopify's fallback.
- `fields` (Map of String) Field key to value, as Shopify serialises metafield values: plain text as is, references as GIDs, booleans and numbers as strings, list types as a JSON array string (use `jsondecode()`). Fields without a value are null entries, so `fields["key"]` works for every field of the definition. A field's type comes from `shopify_metaobject_definition`.
- `id` (String) Metaobject GID, what references take.
- `status` (String) `ACTIVE` or `DRAFT` when the definition has the publishable capability; null otherwise.
- `updated_at` (String) When the entry was last updated (RFC 3339).
